description: Film/TV production, post-production/VFX, publishing, design agencies, music production, games, content creators, entertainment
typical_workflows: Content creation: Texts, graphics, videos, audio, social media posts
Campaign planning: Conception and execution for clients
Project management: Briefing, conception, production, delivery
Creative process: Ideation, moodboards, drafts, feedback
Asset management: Organize media, archive, retrieve
Story development: outline, treatment, script, pitch material
Virtual production: real-time engines, LED volumes, pre-viz
Localization/versioning: subtitles, dubbing, per-channel format adaptation
common_pain_points: Content production is time-consuming: 5-10 hours per week just for social media
Creative blocks: Constantly needing to generate new ideas
Many feedback loops: 3-5 revision rounds per project
Reporting takes time: Monthly reports for each client
Multi-channel complexity: Each channel has different formats/requirements
Trend monitoring: Constantly staying up to date
AI rights uncertainty: usability of AI output, training on protected material, missing clauses in legacy contracts
Labeling obligation: EU AI Act Art. 50 requires transparency for synthetic content (deepfake rule)
Commission budget pressure: broadcasters/platforms already expect AI efficiency in the calculation
ai_opportunities: Content generation: Blog articles, social posts, ad copies via GPT
Image generation: Visuals for social media with DALL-E/Midjourney
Video scripts: Automatically create storyboards and voiceover texts
Automatic reporting: Data from analytics → Formatted report
Trend research: Automatic industry analyses and competitor monitoring
A/B test variants: Quickly generate 10+ variants for ads
SEO optimization: Keyword research and content optimization
Idea generation: Concepts, headlines, storylines via AI
Video editing: Automatic rough cuts, transcription
Pre-viz & storyboards: image/video generation for pitches and look development
Voice cloning & dubbing: multilingual exploitation (only with documented speaker consent)
Rough-cut automation: edit suggestions, scene detection, logging
Archive monetization: AI metadata makes footage libraries searchable and licensable
typical_tools: Adobe Creative Suite / Canva for graphics
Video editing: Premiere, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut
Runway / Firefly for generative image and video content
ElevenLabs for synthetic voices and dubbing
Nuke / Unreal Engine for VFX and virtual production

realistic_quick_wins_kmu.description: Binding rules: which AI tools are allowed, how synthetic content is labeled, how consent (voice/likeness) is documented.

success_metrics: Content output: Number of posts/articles per week
Lead generation: MQLs, SQLs per campaign
Project turnaround: Time from briefing to delivery
Production cost per finished minute of content
Localization rate: share of productions exploited in multiple languages
Archive utilization: share of reused/licensed assets

industry_specific_notes.vfx_post: Automate rotoscoping, cleanup, upscaling first; adapt pricing models to AI efficiency
industry_specific_notes.games: AI assets in concept art/QA/dialogue; observe store and publisher disclosure obligations
industry_specific_notes.entertainment_legal: Clarify chain of rights for AI output (training, output, buyout); voice/likeness clones only with explicit consent; EU AI Act Art. 50 labeling of synthetic content

regulatory_notes: EU AI Act Art. 50: transparency/labeling obligations for AI-generated or synthetic content (deepfakes)
Copyright: TDM opt-outs for training, unresolved protectability of pure AI outputs
Personality rights: secure contractual consent for voice/likeness clones (actors, voice artists)
GDPR: audience/user data in personalization and reach measurement
